transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because my eating has been feeling kind of out of control lately. Mostly at night, when I’m by myself. Once I start, it’s like… I know I should stop, I’m literally telling myself to put the food away, but I just don’t. It feels like something kind of takes over.

I know that probably sounds dramatic. I just… I don’t feel like I’m handling it very well.
Can you describe what happens during these episodes? Specifically, do you feel like you’re eating a much larger amount of food than what most people would eat in a similar time period?

Yeah… I mean, I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but on nights after late shifts it can be… a lot more than I’d normally eat.

Like, I might have a whole frozen pizza, and then cereal straight from the box, and then some leftovers, and whatever snacks are in the cabinet. And that can all happen in maybe an hour or two. It’s definitely not something I’d ever eat like that in front of anyone. I know that’s probably more than most people would have in that amount of time.
During these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control what or how much you're eating, even if you want to?

Yeah… I think that’s probably the main thing, honestly. I can start out thinking I’ll just have a little something, but once I’m eating alone at night it sort of feels like I lose the ability to make myself stop.

I’ll be telling myself, like, “Okay, put it away now,” and I don’t. I just keep going. It feels embarrassing to say, but it’s like something takes over for a while.
Do these episodes make you feel very upset, ashamed, or do they interfere with your daily life in any way?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say it’s ruining everything or anything. But it does get to me. I feel really ashamed afterward, and then the next day I’m kind of… not fully there.

There was this one time at work, during a bilingual outreach presentation, and I kept thinking about leaving afterward—like what I was going to do, getting out of there—and I got distracted enough that I stumbled through parts of it. I don’t know if anyone really noticed, but I was worried my coworkers did. It felt pretty embarrassing.
